Transferred DEV averages are estimates for a new input, not measured latency.
Campaign components are shared across arms and must not be summed across rows.
plain_summary: Single-response baselines generate one candidate; best-reconstruction and pooled methods use 16 or 32; specificity and pruning combinations retain their parent N32 workload.
All twelve fixed methods make zero recurring helper calls. Benchmark Luna judging is a separate research expense.
Prefix-generation and transferred AR seconds are amortized filled-batch work estimates, not single-input latency. Capture is per input item, not separately per cell.

VAL candidate, AR, selector and pruning quantities describe shared campaign work once; repeating them beside methods does not charge them once per arm or make AR required for raw/capped/random selection.
CPU task wall-seconds are elapsed task time with stated threads, not CPU-core-seconds. Do not sum nested parent/stage timers or convert GPU seconds into dollars.
review_scope: All source hashes, numeric field meanings, estimated scaling rules, parent cost inclusion and shared-campaign nonadditivity reviewed; no quality outcomes or final-method decision implied.
